entities.name: Subacute thyroiditis
observations: Often follows a viral respiratory infection and causes transient thyrotoxicosis from release of preformed thyroid hormone, followed by a hypothyroid phase.
Destructive thyroiditis has low or absent radioactive iodine uptake and lacks the persistent hormone synthesis typical of Graves disease.

entities.name: Propylthiouracil
observations: Generally not indicated in subacute thyroiditis because the thyrotoxic phase results from release of stored hormone rather than increased synthesis.
Should be discontinued when the patient transitions to the hypothyroid phase.

entities.name: Propranolol
observations: Can provide symptomatic control during the thyrotoxic phase of subacute thyroiditis but should be stopped when tachycardia and other thyrotoxic symptoms resolve.

entities.name: Transient hypothyroid phase
observations: A TSH increase from 0.03 to 6.0 mIU/L with fatigue one week after treatment is consistent with transition into the hypothyroid phase of subacute thyroiditis.
Repeat TSH and free T4 after a short interval; levothyroxine is generally reserved for overt, persistent, or severe symptomatic hypothyroidism.
